metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VLC Media > Open Network Stream, entered the Apple HLS URL, and clicked Play. Video streamed successfully.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VLC menus, enter URLs in network stream dialog, start playback, and navigate VLC preferences.
metadata.task_rationale: Chains the streaming objective with a VLC preferences change: disable the background cone icon (Tools > Preferences > All > Interface > Main interfaces > Qt > uncheck 'Display background cone or art'). Partial credit: 0.5 per sub-goal.
metadata.explanation: Getter reads vlc-qt-interface.conf for recent MRL (stream check) and vlcrc for qt-bgcone value (cone check). Metric awards 0.5 for URL in recent MRL and 0.5 for qt-bgcone=0. Default qt-bgcone=1, so initial state scores 0.

scoring_breakdown.stream_opened: 0.5 - Apple HLS URL appears in VLC recent MRL list

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements are verified: (1) the HLS stream URL is checked via recent MRL list in vlc-qt-interface.conf, (2) the background cone setting is checked via qt-bgcone in vlcrc.
Negative control resistance is strong: default qt-bgcone=1 means initial state scores 0.0 on the cone sub-goal, and the URL will not appear in recent MRL until the stream is opened.
Partial credit (0.5 per sub-goal) is semantically appropriate for a two-objective composed task.
Getter correctly falls back to qt-bgcone='1' (VLC default) when the key is absent from vlcrc, preventing false positives.
Substring check for expected_url in the comma-separated recent MRL list is the correct approach for VLC URL verification.
Error handling in getter returns an error dict which is caught in the metric (returns 0.0), preventing spurious passes.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: vlcrc is only written when VLC saves preferences or exits. If evaluation runs while VLC is still open and unsaved, qt-bgcone may not yet be persisted. Consider adding a postconfig step to kill/flush VLC or confirm the agent saves preferences before evaluation.

Minor: The recent MRL check confirms the URL was opened at some point but does not confirm active playback at evaluation time. This is the standard approach for VLC and acceptable given the task wording ('open the stream').
